INDEPENDENT ROUTE WARNINGS · NMO 45674
Calbindin-positive glycinergic Renshaw interneuron is one independent NeuroMorpho source object, not an average, archetype, molecular cluster, SCI entity, or morphology transferred from another record.
The repository reports a 50 micrometre horizontal section, whereas the paper reports 400 micrometre transverse recording slices followed by 50 micrometre serial resectioning; these stages must not be collapsed into one preparation claim.
The source reports Dendrites & Axon Moderate; the observed type-2 axon and dendrites are incomplete and cannot establish a complete projection or whole-cell arbor.
The standardized SWC contains 8 type-1 soma points. No native contour-to-SWC mapping is asserted, and these points are not a membrane, nucleus, or volumetric soma segmentation.
Source-authorized radii permit a deterministic radius-derived display surface, but that surface is not an observed membrane, a segmentation, or an independent morphometric measurement.
Identity wording is limited to official_metadata_calbindin_positive_premotor_glycinergic_Renshaw; no cross-study transcriptomic, peptide-abundance, or receptor-distribution identity is created.
No object-level strain conflict was identified, but the unresolved Male/Female repository field is not an individual-sex assignment.
The primary paper does not expose NeuroMorpho ID 45674 or filename 101029p2-A-In, so paper-level paired recordings, contact counts, conductances, and simulations cannot be assigned to this deposited object.
The original Neurolucida DAT is checksum-pinned as a provenance object but has no validated parser or admitted semantic objects in this release; apparent native annotations cannot be promoted to boutons, contacts, or synapses.
Missing same-specimen membrane, nucleus, organelle, synapse, receptor-distribution, and ultrastructure evidence renders zero internal primitives.
Source-local display scaling creates no atlas registration, cross-source identity, relationship to another route, or prevalence estimate.
